---
title: "Website search"
---

## Overview

Every Quarto website and book gets a search box. Rendering the site
builds a full-text index of its pages next to the HTML output, and the
search box in the navbar (or the sidebar) queries it in the browser;
no server, no third-party service, nothing to configure. Results are
grouped by page, show the matching section with a highlighted excerpt,
and following one highlights the search term on the target page.

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
website:
  title: "My Site"
  navbar:
    left:
      - index.qmd
      - docs/guide.qmd
```

That configuration already has search. Set `website.search: false` to
turn it off.

The configuration surface is Quarto 1's, so an existing
`website.search` block carries over unchanged. What differs is the
engine: Quarto 1 downloaded the whole index on the first keystroke and
scanned it with Fuse.js; Quarto 2 builds a [Pagefind](https://pagefind.app)
index that the browser fetches in small pieces as you type, so large
sites stay fast and nothing is downloaded until the reader focuses the
box. See [Differences from Quarto 1](#differences-from-quarto-1).

## Options

```yaml
website:
  search:
    location: navbar          # navbar | sidebar
    type: overlay             # overlay | textbox
    limit: 50
    collapse-after: 3         # or false
    copy-button: false
    keyboard-shortcut: ["f", "/", "s"]
    show-item-context: false  # tree | parent | root | true | false
    merge-navbar-crumbs: true
    search-json: false        # true when algolia is configured
```

| Option | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `location` | `navbar` when the site has a navbar, else `sidebar` | Where the search box lives. |
| `type` | `overlay` in the navbar, `textbox` in the sidebar | `overlay` shows an icon that opens a search dialog; `textbox` shows an inline input with a drop-down panel (it becomes the dialog on narrow screens). |
| `limit` | `50` | Maximum number of matching sections shown. |
| `collapse-after` | `3` | Rows shown per page before a "more matches" toggle; `false` shows every match. |
| `copy-button` | `false` | Adds a button that copies a link to the current search. |
| `keyboard-shortcut` | `f`, `/`, `s` | Keys that open the search box when focus is not in a form field. A single key or a list. |
| `show-item-context` | `false` | Shows where a page sits in the sidebar: `tree` (the full trail; `true` means this), `parent`, or `root`. |
| `merge-navbar-crumbs` | `true` | Prefixes the trail with the navbar item that leads to the page's sidebar. |
| `search-json` | `true` when [`algolia`](#algolia) is configured, else `false` | Writes `search.json`, Quarto 1's record array, at the site root. See [Output files](#output-files). |

The navbar and sidebar can each override the placement:

```yaml
website:
  navbar:
    search: false     # no box in the navbar even when location is navbar
  sidebar:
    search: true      # a textbox in the sidebar
```

An unknown option or a value of the wrong kind is reported
([Q-5-38](../../errors/project/Q-5-38.qmd),
[Q-5-39](../../errors/project/Q-5-39.qmd)) and the default is used; a
search configuration problem never fails a render.

## What gets indexed

Every rendered HTML page, as the reader sees it: body text, headings,
tables, callouts, code and its output. [Drafts](drafts.qmd) (unless
their `draft-mode` is `visible`) and the `404.html` page are left out. To keep a page out of the index without hiding it, set
`search: false` in its front matter:

```yaml
---
title: "Internal notes"
search: false
---
```

Each page is indexed once with its level-2 sections as sub-results, so
a hit inside `## Installation` links straight to that heading. The
page's `lang` picks the stemmer (English when unset): a search for
"rendering" also finds "render" and "rendered".

Search is typo-sensitive: a misspelled word matches nothing. Prefixes
do match while you type.

## Output files

Rendering writes, under the output directory:

- `site_libs/quarto-search/pagefind/` — the index and its runtime.
  The index is split into chunks named by content hash; a query
  fetches only the chunks for the words it contains, a few tens of
  kilobytes each.
- `site_libs/quarto-search/manifest.json` — the site title, the
  Quarto and Pagefind versions that built the index, its languages,
  and the page count. Other sites read it before federating (below).
- `search.json`, only when `search-json` is on (by default, when
  [Algolia](#algolia) is configured) — one record per page and per
  section, in the shape Quarto 1 produced. The search box does not use
  it; it exists for uploading to Algolia and for tools that read it.
  Set `search-json: true` to get it without Algolia, or
  `search-json: false` to skip it even with Algolia (for example,
  when the Algolia index is populated some other way). On a large
  site the file can be bigger than the whole Pagefind index, and
  building it takes render time, so leave it off unless something
  reads it.

When `search.json` is turned off, a copy left by an earlier render is
removed if it is unchanged since Quarto wrote it. A `search.json` that
you have edited, or that Quarto did not write, is left in place.

Incremental renders keep the pages they skipped in the index and drop
sections a page no longer has.

## Searching other sites

A site can extend its search box to other Quarto websites, so an
umbrella documentation site finds pages in the product sites it links
to:

```yaml
website:
  search:
    federate:
      - url: https://docs.example.org/product-a/
        title: Product A         # shown on each result from that site
        weight: 0.8              # rank its results a little lower
      - url: https://docs.example.org/product-b/
      - url: https://other.example.org/
        bundle: pagefind/        # a Pagefind site that is not a Quarto site
```

Each entry names a site's root URL; `title` and `weight` are optional
(the title defaults to the other site's own). Searching queries every
site at once and merges the results; cards from another site carry its
title.

Requirements:

- **Same Pagefind version.** A federated site's index must have been
  built with the same Pagefind version as this site's runtime. Quarto
  checks the other site's `manifest.json` before merging and skips the
  site with a message in the browser console when the versions differ.
  Sites rendered by the same Quarto release always match.
- **Cross-origin access.** Sites under one origin (such as
  `docs.example.org/product-a/` reached from `docs.example.org`) need
  nothing. A site on another origin must serve its
  `site_libs/quarto-search/` directory with an
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header that admits the searching site;
  `quarto preview --static` does this for local development.
- A `bundle` path is only needed for a Pagefind site that is not a
  Quarto website; Quarto sites are found through their fixed
  `site_libs/quarto-search/` location.

Expect each federated site to cost roughly what the local index costs
per query. A dozen sites is comfortable; hundreds would not be.

## Algolia

To query an [Algolia](https://www.algolia.com) index instead of the
built-in one, provide the three connection values:

```yaml
website:
  search:
    algolia:
      index-name: my-site
      application-id: ABC123DEF4
      search-only-api-key: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
      show-logo: true            # "Search by Algolia" footer
      analytics-events: false    # send view/click events to Algolia Insights
      params:                    # extra query parameters
        hitsPerPage: 20
      index-fields:              # if your records use other field names
        text: body
```

With a complete `algolia` block, Quarto also renders `search.json`;
upload it to populate the index (each record has an `objectID`). To
get the file before you have the connection values, set
`search-json: true`. A block missing any of the three
required values is reported as [Q-5-40](../../errors/project/Q-5-40.qmd)
and ignored, so the page keeps the built-in search.

The Algolia client and, with `analytics-events`, the Insights scripts
load from `cdn.jsdelivr.net`. Quarto 2 has no cookie-consent feature
yet, so the Insights scripts are not consent-gated.

## Hosting notes

- The search runtime runs WebAssembly. A Content Security Policy must
  allow `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` in `script-src` and, unless the page
  disables workers, `blob:` in `worker-src`.
- Search needs a web server; it does not work from a `file://` URL.
  The box then shows an error card instead of results.
- `quarto preview` (the default, browser-rendered preview) renders one
  page at a time and shows no search box; `quarto preview --static`
  and a rendered site do.

## Differences from Quarto 1

- The engine is Pagefind, not Fuse.js. Results are ranked by relevance
  with stemming per language, and only the index chunks a query needs
  are downloaded. The trade-off is typo tolerance: Quarto 1's fuzzy
  matching (at its near-exact threshold) is gone.
- `search.json` keeps its shape, but the search box no longer reads
  it, and it is written only when Algolia is configured. **If something
  else on your site reads `search.json`** (a custom search page, a
  script, a deploy step), set `website.search.search-json: true` (or
  `book.search.search-json: true`) to keep getting it.
- `limit` defaults to 50 and `collapse-after` to 3, which is what
  Quarto 1's code did (its documentation said 20 and 2).
- Level-1 sections no longer lose the text between their heading and
  the first level-2 heading, and incremental renders no longer leave
  stale section anchors behind.
- Federated search across sites is new.
